verses.text: So the men of Kiriath Jearim came and took the box of the LORD up to Abinadab's house on the hill. They set apart his son Eleazar to guard the box of the LORD.
The box stayed at Kiriath Jearim a long time, twenty years in all. And all the people of Israel turned back to the LORD with sorrow.

Samuel said to all the people of Israel, "If you are really coming back to the LORD with all your hearts, get rid of the foreign gods and the Ashtoreths among you. Give yourselves completely to the LORD and serve him only, and he will save you from the Philistines."
So the Israelites got rid of their Baals and Ashtoreths and served the LORD only.
Then Samuel said, "Gather all Israel at Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD for you."

When they had gathered at Mizpah, they drew water and poured it out before the LORD. That day they went without food and confessed, "We have sinned against the LORD." Samuel was leading Israel as judge at Mizpah.
When the Philistines heard that Israel had gathered at Mizpah, their rulers came up to attack them. When the Israelites heard about it, they were afraid of the Philistines.
They said to Samuel, "Do not stop crying out to the LORD our God for us, so that he will save us from the Philistines."
Then Samuel took a young lamb and offered it whole as a burnt offering to the LORD. He cried out to the LORD for Israel, and the LORD answered him.

While Samuel was offering the burnt offering, the Philistines came near to attack Israel. But that day the LORD thundered with loud thunder against the Philistines and threw them into such panic that they were defeated by Israel.
The men of Israel rushed out of Mizpah and chased the Philistines, striking them down all the way to a place below Beth Kar.
Then Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen. He named it Ebenezer, which means Stone of Help, saying, "Until now the LORD has helped us."
So the Philistines were defeated, and they stopped coming into Israel's land. As long as Samuel lived, the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines.

The towns the Philistines had taken from Israel, from Ekron to Gath, were given back to Israel, and Israel took back the land around them from the Philistines. There was also peace between Israel and the Amorites.
Samuel continued as Israel's judge all the days of his life.
Every year he travelled around from Bethel to Gilgal to Mizpah, judging Israel in all those places.
Then he would go back to Ramah, where his home was, and he led Israel from there too. And he built an altar there to the LORD.
